title: plugin-auth: an invitation mail sent outside a better-auth endpoint still carries the mailbox proof (mint from the manager's own auth context; blocks cloud#4470)
body:
repo:cloud#1 · os-warren · session_01JQwxbYK6SZCmyzbGnrvmkk

**Follow-up to objectstack#34257 / PR #34333** (one-step invitation acceptance). It was found by the cloud#4470 build thread at objectstack `b1da9f55db`.

## What happens

PR #34333 mints the mailbox proof that an invitation mail carries (deliver-only, never stored) inside the plugin's send path. It mints only when the send runs inside a better-auth endpoint context. A host that calls the plugin's `sendInvitationEmail` from its own code, outside any endpoint, gets no proof, so that mail carries the plain link and the one-step door cannot be used from it.

On the hosted control plane this is the invitation an environment sends on a member's behalf (cloud `member-requests.ts`, cloud#4467). Invitations sent from the console are not affected: they run inside the endpoint and carry the proof today.

The host cannot fix this cleanly from outside:
- `runWithEndpointContext` lives in `@better-auth/core/context`, and `plugin-auth` exports neither that runner nor its proof minting;
- a host-side direct `@better-auth/core` dependency would be a second copy that the host's pin bump does not keep in step.

## Ask

When `mintProofForSend` (or its equivalent) finds no endpoint context, it falls back to the auth manager's own context (`getAuthContext().internalAdapter`) and mints the proof the same way. That way every caller of the plugin's `sendInvitationEmail` gets a mail with the proof. Nothing else changes: the proof is still deliver-only and never stored, and the closing rule (`oneStepSignInState`) still decides what the door does.

## Done when

- A test calls `sendInvitationEmail` outside any endpoint context. The delivered mail carries a proof that the one-step door redeems, and no stored mail row holds the proof.
- The existing in-endpoint path is unchanged (CONTROL).

## Then

cloud#4470 needs no cloud wiring for environment-originated invitations once a release the cloud pins carries this. Its PR ships the console-invite path now, with `Part of #4470`, and names this card as what remains.

## Related

objectstack#34257, PR #34333, cloud#4470, cloud#4467, cloud#4465.
